cultivates.why: Dharma defined as friendship to all
Devotion to others' good

commentary.reading: Tuladhara the merchant to the proud ascetic Jajali.
commentary.source: Tuladhara-Jajali samvada, Shanti Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Mental suffering has only two sources: confusion of the mind or the arrival of something unwanted.

heals.why: Sorts the pain into what happened and what the mind is adding
Names chitta-vibhrama as a cause

cultivates.why: Asking which of the two this is

commentary.reading: Ashma to Janaka.
commentary.source: Ashma Gita, Shanti Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Steady the mind by asking where one was, where one goes, who one is, and why one grieves.

heals.why: Opens grief out into larger questions
Inquiry in place of spinning

cultivates.why: Who am I is asked directly
Self-inquiry as a steadying practice

needs: Some distance from the first shock of loss

commentary.reading: Ashma's practice for sthapana of the mind.
commentary.source: Ashma Gita, Shanti Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: No one obtains unending togetherness with anyone, not even with one's own body.

heals.why: Even the body is a temporary companion
Loss of another is set beside the certain loss of one's own body

cultivates.why: No bond was ever permanent

commentary.reading: Ashma to Janaka.
commentary.source: Ashma Gita, Shanti Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Fruit drops from the tree, but a father does not let go of his child even while suffering through love.

depicts.why: A parent's holding on, named with tenderness

cultivates.why: What a father carries for a child

commentary.reading: Chirakari weighs the father's claim before the mother's.
commentary.source: Chirakari upakhyana, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One who still has a mother to lean on lives like a small child even at a hundred.

cultivates.why: Having a mother alive is named as a shelter one still has

commentary.reading: Chirakari's praise of the mother.
commentary.source: Chirakari upakhyana, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: A mother protects her child whether he is capable or not, and no one else nurtures as she does.

heals.why: One was loved regardless of capability

cultivates.why: Her care does not depend on the child's success

commentary.reading: Chirakari's praise of the mother.
commentary.source: Chirakari upakhyana, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Jealousy brings ruin even to ascetics; it threw me into a sea of wrongdoing.

depicts.why: Gautama speaks in remorse over what jealousy made him order
Irshya named by the one it overcame

heals.why: Even a disciplined sage fell to this, and saw it

commentary.reading: Gautama's own confession on returning.
commentary.source: Chirakari upakhyana, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One who deliberates and decides slowly in every matter does not suffer long regret.

heals.why: Slowness in deciding is approved

cultivates.why: Deliberate first

commentary.reading: Bhishma's moral of the Chirakari story.
commentary.source: Chirakari upakhyana, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: You, I and all beings will die without escaping joy and sorrow, so what is there to lament?

heals.why: The loss is placed in the common lot of all

cultivates.why: No one is exempt

commentary.reading: Narada to Srinjaya, whose son has died; the Shodasha-rajakiya follows, and the son is restored at the end.
commentary.source: Shodasha-rajakiya, Shanti Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: 'You're not alone in this' replaces 'so why lament'. Honest version: 'You, I and every creature will die, none of us free of joy and sorrow. This is shared by all.'

claim: One who withstands the surges of speech, anger, ambition, hunger and lust when they rise is the true sage.

heals.why: Anger is treated as a wave that can be ridden out
Urges are forces that pass

cultivates.why: Withstanding the surge

commentary.reading: The Hamsa on vega-dharana.
commentary.source: Hamsa Gita, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Fault-finders are far more eager to speak of a person's flaws than of his good qualities.

depicts.why: The experience of hearing only one's flaws discussed

heals.why: The imbalance is shown to be the critic's habit, not a measure of the person

cultivates.why: Criticism weighed for its source

commentary.reading: The Hamsa on those who hunt for faults.
commentary.source: Hamsa Gita, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Whatever an angry person gives, sacrifices or practises is carried off by Yama; his labour is wasted.

heals.why: Anger is shown cancelling one's own good work

commentary.reading: The Hamsa on krodha as the destroyer of merit.
commentary.source: Hamsa Gita, Shanti Parva Mokshadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Guard austerity from anger, fortune from envy, learning from pride and insult, and oneself from heedlessness.

heals.why: Named as what eats discipline
Named as what eats good fortune
Named as the threat to oneself

cultivates.why: Four things to protect, each from its own enemy

commentary.reading: Sanatkumara's counsel relayed by Narada to Shuka.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: One should not grieve alone over a trouble shared by all, but act to remedy it if a way is seen.

heals.why: Shared trouble is taken off one person's shoulders
Grieving is replaced by looking for the remedy

cultivates.why: Act where a way appears

commentary.reading: Narada to Shuka: where effort is possible, effort and not grief.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: People who reach one level of wealth after another stay unsatisfied and are ruined; the wise reach contentment.

depicts.why: Each level reached and still not enough

heals.why: Shows the ladder has no top

cultivates.why: The wise step off it

commentary.reading: Narada to Shuka on atripti.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Thirst has no end and contentment is the highest happiness, so the wise regard contentment as wealth.

heals.why: No end to wanting is stated flatly
Wealth is redefined

cultivates.why: Contentment as the real wealth

commentary.reading: Narada to Shuka.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Life does not stand still even for a blink, so why dwell on perishable bodies as if they were lasting?

heals.why: Brooding is set against how fast life moves
The body is not a lasting thing to anchor on

cultivates.why: Impermanence seen in one's own body

commentary.reading: Narada to Shuka on anityata.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

line_issue: 'Don't spend it brooding' is looser than the verse. Closer: 'Life does not pause, not even for the blink of an eye. In a body that is passing, what is there to hold as permanent?'

claim: Fathers strive and mothers fast, vow and carry a child ten months, wishing every good for their children.

cultivates.why: Lists what parents did before one could know it

commentary.reading: In context Yudhishthira is mourning the slain young men and the parents whose hopes died with them; the library uses it as a verse on parental care.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: When one is wronged by others, kinsmen are the refuge, for kin never tolerate the humiliation of kin.

heals.why: One does not have to carry an insult alone
One's own people will stand with one

cultivates.why: Trust in family as shelter

needs: That the wrong came from outside the family

commentary.reading: Bhishma weighs kinsmen: they are a source of trouble and also the one refuge when outsiders insult you. Must not be shown to someone wronged at home.
commentary.source: Plain sense of the verse as in the Gita Press Hindi Mahabharata; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: When kinsmen are ready to speak bitter or petty words, calm their hearts and minds with your own speech.

heals.why: A specific task in a family quarrel: cool it with words

cultivates.why: Answering bitterness with calming speech
Speech as the peacemaker's tool

commentary.reading: Narada to Krishna as head of the clan.
commentary.source: Vasudeva-Narada samvada, Shanti Parva Rajadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: The harsh words of my own kin churn my heart like a fire stick and burn me every day.

depicts.why: Krishna says plainly that his relatives' words burn him daily
Worn down by family strife

commentary.reading: Krishna's own confession to Narada. That even he says this is what makes it a Day 1 verse.
commentary.source: Vasudeva-Narada samvada, Shanti Parva Rajadharma; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: Line generalises and comments. Keep his voice: 'The harsh words of my own people burn me every day, as a fire stick is churned for fire.'

claim: One who seeks well-being should never slander, speak unpleasantly or provoke anyone's anger.

cultivates.why: Speech that does not wound or provoke

commentary.reading: Achara rules.
commentary.source: Bhishma on achara (conduct for a long life), Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: An aged relative, a friend, an unsupported sister, a teacher and the worthy poor should be sheltered as one is able.

cultivates.why: Housing and protecting those who depend on one
Care within one's means

commentary.reading: Achara: giving such people a home is called dhanya and ayushya.
commentary.source: Bhishma on achara (conduct for a long life), Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One free of anger, truthful, harmless, without envy and straight lives a hundred years.

cultivates.why: Harmlessness and freedom from envy
A life without anger

commentary.reading: Achara; a generic promise of long life.
commentary.source: Bhishma on achara (conduct for a long life), Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One should never taunt people for bodily difference, lack of learning, age, looks, poverty or standing.

heals.why: For one mocked for body, money or schooling, the text is on their side

cultivates.why: No one is to be mocked for what they lack

commentary.reading: Achara.
commentary.source: Bhishma on achara (conduct for a long life), Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One should rise before the sun and first greet mother, father and teacher; this brings long life.

cultivates.why: A daily act of respect to parents
A fixed start to the day

commentary.reading: Achara.
commentary.source: Bhishma on achara (conduct for a long life), Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: 'Small daily respect adds up to a good life' is commentary. Closer: 'Rise before the sun, and greet your mother and father first. This is how a long life is won.'

claim: A father should never give his sons unequal shares.

heals.why: For a child given less, the text says the unequal share was wrong

commentary.reading: A rule of fair partition among undivided brothers.
commentary.source: Bhishma on elder and younger brothers, Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; text of this passage varies between recensions

line_issue: 'Unequal shares plant resentment for a generation' is invented. Corrected: 'When a family's property is divided, a parent should never give unequal shares.'

claim: The elder should at times act blind or slow though wise, and point out a younger one's lapse indirectly.

heals.why: Not every lapse needs a confrontation

cultivates.why: Overlooking on purpose
Correct by indirection

commentary.reading: Counsel to the eldest brother who holds the family together.
commentary.source: Bhishma on elder and younger brothers, Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; text of this passage varies between recensions

claim: Enemies who burn at a family's prosperity seek to divide brothers; those who stay united are not broken.

cultivates.why: Watchfulness about who profits from a family split

commentary.reading: Text is uncertain here, with a bracketed variant line.
commentary.source: Bhishma on elder and younger brothers, Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; text of this passage varies between recensions

claim: The eldest can raise or ruin a family, and it is usually his lack of humility that ruins it.

heals.why: Arrogance in the one who leads is named as the family-breaker

commentary.reading: Durvinaya, want of discipline and humility, in the jyeshtha.
commentary.source: Bhishma on elder and younger brothers, Anushasana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; text of this passage varies between recensions

claim: Desire says that whoever tries to destroy it with some weapon finds it reborn in that very weapon.

heals.why: Explains why force and suppression keep failing
Relapse is how desire works, not a personal defect

cultivates.why: The means of fighting desire can become its new seat

commentary.reading: Kama Gita: desire reappears as desire for the vow, the austerity, the merit, even for moksha. Krishna's point is that it is overcome by dropping mamatva, not by a weapon.
commentary.source: Kama Gita, Ashvamedhika Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One who owns the earth without 'mine' is unharmed by it; a forest dweller who clings to possessions is in death's jaws.

heals.why: Bondage is in the clinging, not in the having

cultivates.why: Letting go inwardly while keeping one's place in life
Outer renunciation is not the test

commentary.reading: Krishna dissuading Yudhishthira from the forest: what binds is mamata. A direct counterweight to verses that push withdrawal.
commentary.source: Kama Gita context, Ashvamedhika Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: 'A mansion can be light, a hut heavy' invents images. Corrected: 'A person may hold the whole earth and be free, if nothing in it is mine. A person may live in the forest and be bound, if he clings to what he has.'

claim: Seeing greed for what it is, restrain it with steadiness and seek rule over oneself, the only real kingdom.

heals.why: Greed is the last enemy standing after outer victories

cultivates.why: Restraint by steadiness
The self rightly known is the king

commentary.reading: Ambarisha's gatha in the Anugita.
commentary.source: Anugita, Ashvamedhika Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: I made every effort for peace with the Kauravas, but they could not be brought to it.

depicts.why: The one who tried for peace is now being blamed for the rupture

heals.why: Having truly tried, the failure of peace is not one's fault

cultivates.why: Standing by an honest effort

commentary.reading: Krishna to the angry sage Uttanka: he tried conciliation fully and they refused. Peace needs both sides.
commentary.source: Uttanka upakhyana, Ashvamedhika Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Hunger drives out wisdom, the sense of dharma and steadiness.

heals.why: Loss of judgement under real want is explained, not condemned

cultivates.why: Understanding for those acting from need

commentary.reading: Said in the tale of the gleaner's family, who gave their only food while starving; the verse states how hard that was.
commentary.source: Nakula (mongoose) upakhyana, Ashvamedhika Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: 'Be gentle with yourself and others when money is tight' is invented. Corrected: 'Hunger drives out good sense, pushes aside the feeling for what is right, and wears away steadiness.'

claim: Dharma is pleased less by lavish gifts than by small ones justly earned and given in faith.

heals.why: Small means do not make a small offering
Scale is not the measure

cultivates.why: What is honestly one's own is enough to give
Sincerity is what counts

commentary.reading: Moral of the gleaner's gift of flour.
commentary.source: Nakula (mongoose) upakhyana, Ashvamedhika Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: In deciding dharma, weigh the heavier against the lighter and choose where the greater good lies.

heals.why: A method for a clash of duties: weigh and take the weightier

cultivates.why: Guru-laghava, comparing weights

commentary.reading: The hawk says this to make Shibi hand over the dove. Shibi accepts the weighing but keeps his refuge-duty and offers his own flesh. The principle is sound; the speaker is using it to tempt.
commentary.source: Shibi upakhyana, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Growth is not measured by bodily size; the small tree that bears fruit is the grown one.

heals.why: Worth is measured by fruit, not size or seniority

cultivates.why: Standing on what one can actually do

commentary.reading: Ashtavakra to the gatekeeper who bars him as a child.
commentary.source: Ashtavakriya, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Dharma cannot be known without study and attending on elders, even by one as wise as Brihaspati.

heals.why: Cleverness alone is not enough

cultivates.why: Learning from those who have lived it
Respect for elders' experience

commentary.reading: Hanuman to Bhima after humbling him.
commentary.source: Hanuman-Bhima samvada, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Riding the heavens and drunk with pride, I gave no thought to anyone else.

depicts.why: Nahusha describes his own intoxication with success
Said looking back from the fall

heals.why: Hearing it confessed makes it visible in oneself

commentary.reading: Nahusha's confession: abhimana made him yoke the sages to his palanquin, and Agastya's curse followed.
commentary.source: Ajagara parva (Nahusha-Yudhishthira samvada), Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Truth, self-restraint, austerity, non-harm and constant learning make a person good, not birth or family.

heals.why: Worth does not come from birth or background

cultivates.why: Standing rests on conduct

commentary.reading: The epic's clear statement that conduct, not jati or kula, makes the good person.
commentary.source: Ajagara parva (Nahusha-Yudhishthira samvada), Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Sometimes truth outweighs giving and sometimes giving outweighs truth; the weight depends on the case.

heals.why: Virtues are not ranked once for all

cultivates.why: Weigh by the situation

commentary.reading: Yudhishthira on the relative weight of virtues.
commentary.source: Ajagara parva (Nahusha-Yudhishthira samvada), Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: A fool does not shine by praising himself, while a truly learned person shines even unadorned.

heals.why: Self-promotion does not produce worth
Real ability shows without polish

cultivates.why: No need to advertise

commentary.reading: Shishtachara.
commentary.source: Vyadha Gita, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: The conduct of the good has three steps: betray no one, give, and always speak truth.

cultivates.why: Never betray
Give

commentary.reading: Shishtachara in three padas.
commentary.source: Vyadha Gita, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: The secret of the Veda is truth, of truth self-restraint, and of self-restraint letting go.

cultivates.why: Tyaga as the innermost of the three
A ladder from truth to restraint to release

commentary.reading: Upanishad here means the inner secret or essence.
commentary.source: Vyadha Gita, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: Line says 'wisdom' for Veda; acceptable, but 'the Veda' is what the verse names.

claim: One free of envy and grateful keeps to the good and gains happiness, dharma, prosperity and heaven.

heals.why: Freedom from envy is tied to happiness

cultivates.why: Gratitude named as a source of well-being

commentary.reading: Shishtachara.
commentary.source: Vyadha Gita, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: An anxious person has no peace and no happiness, and a husband is never truly won by charms.

heals.why: Control breeds the very fear that ends closeness

cultivates.why: A bond rests on trust, not control

commentary.reading: Draupadi tells Satyabhama that a husband who suspects charms fears his wife like a snake in the house. The chapter around it lays out a wife's duties of service, so only this point travels.
commentary.source: Draupadi-Satyabhama samvada, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: 'Love has nowhere to grow' is invented. Corrected: 'Where one person feels managed, there is no peace, and without peace there is no happiness. No one is truly won by tricks.' Do not surface the chapter's other verses.

claim: Those who offend through lack of understanding should be forgiven, since wisdom is not easily found in everyone.

heals.why: Sees the offender's limitation

cultivates.why: A named case for forgiveness
Allowance for ignorance

needs: The whole list, including when not to forgive

commentary.reading: One of Prahlada's occasions for kshama, quoted by Draupadi before she turns to the occasions for tejas: the deliberate and repeated offender is not to be forgiven.
commentary.source: Draupadi-Yudhishthira samvada, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: One who restrains arisen anger by wisdom is the one the wise call truly powerful.

heals.why: Catching anger as it rises is called strength

cultivates.why: Prajna as the check
Power redefined as mastery of anger

commentary.reading: Yudhishthira redefines tejas against Draupadi's call for force; one side of the debate.
commentary.source: Yudhishthira's praise of kshama in the Draupadi-Yudhishthira samvada, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Forgiveness is Brahman, truth, austerity and purity, and it upholds the world.

cultivates.why: Forbearance praised as the ground of everything

commentary.reading: Kashyapa's gatha quoted by Yudhishthira. Praise poetry for kshama; the same book has Prahlada's limit on it.
commentary.source: Yudhishthira's praise of kshama in the Draupadi-Yudhishthira samvada, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: The wise say friendship is made by walking seven steps together.

cultivates.why: Friendship forms quickly between those who walk together

commentary.reading: Savitri claims friendship with Yama so that he will hear her.
commentary.source: Savitri upakhyana, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Trust is born of goodwill toward all beings, which is why people trust the good above all.

cultivates.why: Goodwill is the root of being trusted
Why the good can be relied on

commentary.reading: Savitri to Yama.
commentary.source: Savitri upakhyana, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: The good work for others' benefit without looking for any return.

heals.why: Helping is freed from waiting for return

cultivates.why: Service without keeping account

commentary.reading: Savitri on the conduct of the noble.
commentary.source: Savitri upakhyana, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Those who only read, teach and ponder scripture are fools; the one who acts on it is learned.

heals.why: Knowing without doing is called out

cultivates.why: Wisdom is located in practice

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna: kriyavan is the pandita.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: A true person is one to whom pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future are alike.

cultivates.why: Evenness named as the mark of the full person

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Non-cruelty is the highest dharma, higher than the greatest gain, so let Nakula live.

depicts.why: Yudhishthira chooses fairness to his other mother over his own advantage

heals.why: A hard choice settled by asking what is kindest and fairest

cultivates.why: Anrishamsya placed above gain

commentary.reading: Offered one brother's life, he picks Nakula so that Madri, like Kunti, keeps a son. The Yaksha then restores all four.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Learning is the friend abroad, a wife at home, the physician in illness, and charity at death.

heals.why: Each condition has its companion, even being far from home

cultivates.why: Names who actually stands by one in each state

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna. The line's 'spouse' for bharya is right.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Competence is the one path to dharma, giving to fame, truth to heaven, and good character to happiness.

cultivates.why: Happiness tied to character

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna; generic.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Austerity is keeping to one's own duty, restraint is taming the mind, forbearance is bearing opposites, shame is turning from wrong.

heals.why: Shame is defined as a turning back from wrong, a working conscience, not self-hatred
Restraint means the mind

cultivates.why: Bearing heat and cold, gain and loss
Plain definitions of four virtues

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna. Kshama here is dvandva-sahishnuta, bearing life's pairs, not bearing a wrongdoer.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

line_issue: The line could use the definition of shame for guilt plans: 'Shame, rightly understood, is simply turning back from what should not be done.'

claim: Knowledge is grasping things as they are, calm is a quiet mind, compassion is wishing happiness for all.

cultivates.why: Calm defined as stillness of mind
Wishing all beings happiness

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna definitions.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Steadiness is firmness in one's duty, fortitude is sense-mastery, the true bath is cleansing the mind, true giving is protecting beings.

cultivates.why: Defined as mastery of the senses
The real bath is washing the mind
Giving defined as protecting life

commentary.reading: Yaksha Prashna definitions.
commentary.source: Yaksha Prashna (Vana Parva); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: The more Nala lost at dice, the more his passion for the game grew.

depicts.why: Compulsion that grows with each loss
He cannot see what everyone around him sees

heals.why: A great king was caught the same way

commentary.reading: Nala, entered by Kali, cannot stop; the tradition reads the compulsion as possession, a force riding him, and he later recovers everything.
commentary.source: Nalopakhyana, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: For a suffering man there is no medicine equal to a wife, in every sorrow.

heals.why: One is not alone in hardship

cultivates.why: The partner who stays is named as the medicine
Companionship in trouble

commentary.reading: Damayanti refusing to leave Nala in the forest. Spoken by the wife of herself.
commentary.source: Nalopakhyana, Vana Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: Sanskrit says 'wife' for an afflicted 'man'; the line's neutral 'partner' should be kept.

claim: Uncontrolled senses can destroy a person, as unbroken horses destroy a poor charioteer.

heals.why: Urges are pictured as horses that need a driver
The undriven mind is dangerous to its owner

cultivates.why: Holding the reins

commentary.reading: Gandhari to Duryodhana; the chariot image is the Katha Upanishad's.
commentary.source: Gandhari's counsel in the Kuru court, Udyoga Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Half the earth is enough to live on; heed your well-wishers and you will gain a good name.

heals.why: Enough is named

cultivates.why: Half suffices
Listen to those who wish you well

commentary.reading: Gandhari urging Duryodhana to share the kingdom.
commentary.source: Gandhari's counsel in the Kuru court, Udyoga Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Take up the yoke and pull like a thoroughbred; summon your courage and self-respect and know your own strength.

heals.why: A direct summons out of collapse
Reminded of the strength already in oneself

cultivates.why: Mana, self-respect, is to be summoned
Lift and pull

commentary.reading: Vidula's call to paurusha.
commentary.source: Vidula-putra-anushasana, Udyoga Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: A king should never show fear in a crisis, and even if shaken should not behave as one shaken.

heals.why: Fear is admitted and still not allowed to steer

cultivates.why: Composure for those who depend on one
Bearing of fearlessness

commentary.reading: Vidula: when the king looks broken, the whole kingdom breaks with him.
commentary.source: Vidula-putra-anushasana, Udyoga Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

line_issue: Line shifts from 'do not show it' to 'do not let fear decide'. Closer: 'In a crisis a leader may be shaken inside, and still must not act like a shaken person. Others take their courage from you.'

claim: Even one who wins the whole earth does not escape old age, death, joy and sorrow.

cultivates.why: Conquest does not exempt anyone from the human lot

commentary.reading: Sanjaya speaks as Dhritarashtra's envoy, urging the robbed Pandavas to drop their claim. Yudhishthira and Krishna answer that this is dharma-talk in the service of injustice.
commentary.source: Sanjaya-yana, Udyoga Parva; plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering

claim: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, good breeding, restraint, learning, valour, few words, giving and gratitude.

cultivates.why: Gratitude is among the eight
Restraint and few words

commentary.reading: Vidura's list.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: The noble do not exult in their own joy, delight in another's sorrow, or regret a gift.

heals.why: No pleasure in another's fall
No gloating

cultivates.why: Goodwill in both one's joy and another's pain

commentary.reading: Vidura's arya-shila.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Sleeplessness comes to one attacked by the stronger, the weak, the resourceless, the robbed, the lustful and the thief.

depicts.why: The sleepless night is the subject

heals.why: Sorts sleeplessness into being overpowered, loss, craving or conscience

commentary.reading: Vidura's first answer when the king says he cannot sleep; he asks, with an edge, which of these the king is.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Before acting, consider what will follow from doing it and from not doing it, then act or refrain.

heals.why: Two questions that settle an undecided mind
Turns worry into a short deliberation

cultivates.why: Weigh both branches

commentary.reading: Vidura on deliberate action.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Envy of others' wealth, beauty, strength, family, happiness or honour is a disease without end.

depicts.why: Lists exactly what envy fixes on

heals.why: Called a disease, something one has and can treat

commentary.reading: Vidura on irshya.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Craving takes patience, envy takes goodness, anger takes fortune, bad company takes character, and pride takes everything.

heals.why: Pride is named the thief of everything
Anger costs prosperity
Expectation wears away patience

commentary.reading: Vidura's list of what steals what; the full verse begins with age taking beauty and death taking life.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: When abused do not abuse in return; the forbearer's held anger burns the abuser and wins his merit.

heals.why: Not answering is shown as the stronger position

cultivates.why: Titiksha under insult

commentary.reading: Atreya's teaching to the Sadhyas as retold by Vidura. The text grants that the forbearer has manyu, and says it works on the abuser by itself.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: A lone tree, however strong, is felled by wind, while trees standing together withstand it by supporting each other.

heals.why: Standing alone is the risk; leaning on others is strength

cultivates.why: Mutual support among one's people

commentary.reading: Vidura on the strength of united kinsmen.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Excessive pride, overtalking, not giving, anger, selfishness and betraying friends are the swords that cut life short.

heals.why: Pride heads the list
Anger as a blade against oneself

commentary.reading: Vidura's answer to why people do not live their full hundred years.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: The forest and its tigers protect each other, and neither survives without the other.

heals.why: Rivals inside a family are shown as each other's protection

cultivates.why: Seeing mutual dependence

commentary.reading: Vidura: the Kauravas are the forest and the Pandavas its tigers.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

line_issue: 'Families that fight forget they protect each other' is a gloss. Corrected: 'No forest without tigers, and no tigers without the forest. Each keeps the other safe.'

claim: One who checks the rising surge of anger and of elation, and keeps clear in calamity, is fit for fortune.

heals.why: Checked as it rises
Elation is checked the same way

cultivates.why: Both surges handled alike
Clear in calamity

commentary.reading: Vidura.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Do not speak of what you intend to do; show only what is done.

cultivates.why: Resolve kept quiet and proved by results
Work before words

commentary.reading: Vidura on guarding counsel.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Even Brihaspati, speaking at the wrong time, meets contempt and disregard.

heals.why: Being dismissed may be about timing, not worth

cultivates.why: Choose the moment to speak

commentary.reading: Vidura on timely speech.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: People wish for a friend who is grateful, righteous, truthful, large-hearted, loyal, self-controlled and steady.

cultivates.why: A portrait of the friend worth having and being
Gratitude is listed first

commentary.reading: Vidura.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

line_issue: 'Be that friend' is added. Drop it or mark it as commentary.

claim: Only one's own deeds follow a person from the pyre, so one should gather dharma carefully, little by little.

heals.why: What lasts is set against what is left behind

cultivates.why: Small daily accumulation of good

commentary.reading: Vidura: karma alone accompanies the dead.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: One who gives up even a great gain joined to wrong sleeps at ease, like a snake freed of its old skin.

heals.why: Shows what the clean choice feels like afterwards
Sleep returns with the tainted gain let go
A great gain can be refused

cultivates.why: Integrity chosen without being forced

commentary.reading: Said to a king who cannot sleep because he is holding what is not his.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: Make steadiness the boat and cross the river whose water is the senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger.

heals.why: Desire named as a crocodile to be passed
Anger likewise

cultivates.why: Steadiness is the vessel

commentary.reading: Vidura's closing imagery.
commentary.source: Vidura Niti (Udyoga Parva, Prajagara); plain sense as in the Gita Press Hindi rendering; Nilakantha's gloss not separately verified

claim: One who respectfully consults a kinsman mature in wisdom, virtue, learning and years is never confused about what to do.

heals.why: One does not have to decide alone
Counsel clears confusion
